4. On receipt of the nominations of the representatives from different member bodies, the Election Board of FBCCI published the preliminary voters' list on 25-6-2007 including the names of BGMEA nominees at serial No. 82 as voter Nos. 386 to 390. After publication of the preliminary voter list, one Mahbub Minhaj, respondent N. 6, submitted an objection dated 30-6-2007 to respondent No.4, that is, the Election Appeal Board, praying for disqualifying the nominated members of the present Executive Committee of BGMEA and from entering them as voters in FBCCI election of 2007-2008. According to him, the legal character and competency of holding the posts of the present Executive Committee was under challenge before the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 116 of 2007. In that suit an application was filed for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from holding BGMEA election of 2007-2008. During the pendency of the suit the plaintiff filed a further application and the learned Assistant Judge granted interim injunction on 22-2-2007 restraining holding of BGMEA election on 25-2-2007 till disposal of the suit. In violation of that order, the election was held on 25-2-2007. By an order dated 11-3-2007, the 1st Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka passed a temporary order of injunction on 11-3-2007 restraining the defendants from handing over the executive power and from holding the AGM (Annual General Meeting) of BGMEA. Against that order of injunction, defendant No. 6 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The Appeal was, however, allowed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka by his order dated 5-6-2007. BGMEA election was, however held as per the revised election schedule on 3-12-2007. After that, Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2007 filed by the plaintiff for violating the order of injunction dated 22-2-2007 has been pending for hearing. The order of injunction dated 11-3-2007 restraining the defendants from holding the AGM of BGMEA or transfer of executive power was not violated. Neither BGMEA nor any -of the members of its outgoing Executive Committee nor the candidates of BGMEA election 2007-2008 nor the General Body of BGMEA or its members were parties to the suit. Defendant No. 6 appealed against the order dated 11-3-2007 passed in the Suit in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 which was allowed by the 6th Court of learned Additional District Judge, Dhaka by its order dated 5-6-2007. The plaintiff filed a revisional application being Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 before this Court whereupon a Rule was issued and the operation of the order appealed against was stayed. 

 7. Respondent No. 1 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of respondent No. 1, in short, is that there is no express bar either in the Ordinance or in the Rules to challenging the legality of the decision of FBCCI Election Appeal Board before the Arbitration Tribunal. Section 12 of the Ordinance gives wide powers to the Tribunal to decide any questions or impropriety relating to election and is expressly made applicable to the present situation. By virtue of Article 13A of the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the FBCCI is legally entitled to reject the nominations of BGMEA and holding the election. Since the validity of BGMEA election is in dispute, the FBCCI is empowered by its Articles of Association to reject the nominations made by BGMEA. FBCCI is an apex trade organisation and is not concerned with the internal affairs/disputes of the members of BGMEA. The dispute relating to the BGMEA election is an internal matter strictly between the members of BGMEA. The FBCCI is not a party to the dispute. The Tribunal is empowered by its Articles to co-opt anyone person from the general members representing BGMEA if the latter fails to file nomination for the post of a nominated director. 

 8. Respondent No. 2 filed an affidavit-in-opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of respondent No. 2, in short, is that the Arbitration Tribunal passed its judgment in accordance with law. It is also stated that the present Writ Petition is not maintainable as it is an unlawful fetter on the statutory obligations of the FBCCI as the apex trade organisation and it is unjustified in all the circumstances of the case advanced by the petitioners in this petition. It is important to mention here that the statements made in its affidavit-in-opposition by this respondent are almost identical to those in the affidavit of respondent No. 6 (FBCCI). 

 9. Respondent No. 6 also filed an affidavit-in- opposition controverting all the material allegations made in the Writ Petition. The case of this respondent, in short, is that on the date of filing of the suit the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) praying for temporary injunction restraining the principal defendants from holding of BGMEA election 2007- 2008. After hearing the plaintiff, the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka directed the principal defendants to show cause as to why an order of temporary injunction should not be granted within one day from the date of receipt of the notice. On 20-2-2007, the plaintiff filed another application under section 151 of the Code praying for an order of ad interim injunction restraining the principal defendants from holding BGMEA election scheduled to be held on 25-2-2007. Since the defendant did not appear within the time prescribed by the Court the learned Assistant Judge passed an order restraining the principal defendants from holding the election scheduled for 25-2-2007. In spite of the order of injunction, the election was held on 25-2-2007. Afterwards, the plaintiff filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) of the Code for wilful violation of the Court's order of injunction in Violation Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2007. On 27-7-2007, the plaintiff again filed an application under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code praying for an injunction restraining the principal defendant Nos. 5-6 from handing over their executive power to the Board of Directors. The learned Assistant Judge directed the principal defendants to show cause within five days. Since the defendant failed to appear, the learned Assistant Judge passed an order restraining the principal defendants from holding AGM on 12-3-2007. On 4-3-2007, defendant No.7 filed written objection against the application filed under Order XXXIX, rules 1 and 2 of the Code. They also filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint. Defendant No.6 appealed against the order dated 11-3-2007 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The Appeal ultimately was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal setting aside the order of injunction passed by the learned Assistant Judge. The plaintiff then filed a revisional application being Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 before this Court. The High Court Division issued Rule and stayed operation of the impugned judgment and order. Because of the pendency of the Civil Suit, the very locus standi of the persons nominated for the election of FBCCI is in dispute and, as such, the Arbitration Tribunal legally allowed the appeal. 

 (3) The findings of the Tribunal that the election of BGMEA was held in violation of the order of injunction dated 22-2-2007 is erroneous before disposal of Violation Miscellaneous. Case No. 16 of 2007. Unless the Violation Case is allowed, it cannot be said that the election was held in violation of the order of injunction. 

 2. Under section 12 of the Ordinance any member of any trade organisation may file an Arbitration Case before the Arbitration Tribunal of FBCCI and in the instant case respondent No. 6 being a member of BGMEA was legally entitled to file the Arbitration Case before the Tribunal as mentioned above. 

 2. Though FBCCI was not made a party in the Arbitration Tribunal Case even then it is bound by order/award given by the Tribunal because the petitioners represent the BGMEA. 

 16. On 22-2-2007, the learned Assistant Judge restrained respondent Nos. 1-6 by an order of injunction from holding BGMEA election scheduled to be held on 25-2-2007. The BGMEA election was, however, held on 25-2-2007. A Miscellaneous Case filed by the plaintiff for violation of the order of injunction under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) of the Code on 27-2-2007 has been pending. On 11-3- 2007, the plaintiff filed another application for injunction restraining the defendants from holding AGM and from transferring power to the elected committee. The application for injunction was allowed as prayed for on that date. The AGM was, however, held and the power was transferred. On 15-3-2007, the plaintiff filed an application for withdrawal of the suit along with other Miscellaneous Cases filed by him. On 25-3-2007, respondent No. 3 filed an application to be added as a plaintiff and the application for addition was allowed. On 26-5-2007, notice inviting trade organisations to nominate members to the general body of the FBCCI for its election scheduled for 16-8-2007 was issued. On 25-6-2007, the preliminary voter list for FBCCI election was published. On 30-6-2007, respondent No. 6 filed an objection to the FBCCI Election Board seeking exclusion of the voters nominated by BGMEA. The appeal was rejected whereupon respondent No.6 filed Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007 before the Arbitration Tribunal of FBCCI. The Tribunal allowed the appeal directing exclusion of all five members nominated by BGMEA from the voter list of FBCCI. 

 17. The Tribunal came to a finding that the election of BGMEA was held in clear violation of the order of stay dated 20-2-2007. This finding of the Tribunal is erroneous on the ground that whether the election was held in violation of the order of stay (in fact, injunction) will be decided in Violation Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 2007. Unless and until the Violation Case is allowed after taking evidence from both the sides, it is premature to say that the election was held in violation of the order of stay dated 22-2-2007. In addition, a Violation Case under Order XXXIX, rule 2(3) is a quasi criminal proceedings which will only be decided upon taking evidence from both the sides. 

 18. Against the order of injunction dated 13-3-2007 restraining the defendants from holding AGM and from transferring executive power till disposal of the suit, defendant No. 7 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 84 of 2007 which was allowed. Against the judgment passed in the Appeal, the plaintiff filed a revisional application before this Court, which issued Rule and stayed the operation of the order passed by the appellate Court in Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007. The Arbitration Tribunal found that the current Executive Committee of BGMEA had been formed without lawful authority and that since the BGMEA Election had taken place in violation of a Court's order and was illegal, the Executive Committee formed by the Board of Directors pursuant to the BGMEA Election was illegal. This finding is also totally misconceived, because whether the Election had taken place in violation of the Court's order could not be decided by the Tribunal which even did not have the jurisdiction to say that the BGMEA Election had taken place in violation of the Court's order until the violation case is allowed and the suit is decreed. Had there been an order of injunction restraining exclusion of the nominations made by BGMEA from being voters of the FBCCI Election, the Tribunal in that event could exclude the voters of the BGMEA. It is contended that the holding of AGM and handing over executive power were not proper during continuance of the order of stay passed by the High Court Division. Whether the AGM and handing over power were done in violation of the order of stay passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2981 of 2007 may be decided in an appropriate proceeding if initiated by the plaintiff-petitioner. The interpretation of the Court's orders by the Tribunal regarding stay and injunction is erroneous and contrary to established principles of law. 

 27. If the aforesaid Articles are considered in juxtaposition, it appears that FBCCI has two types of members (1) Ordinary Member/Member Body (2) General Members to be nominated by the member bodies. Now it is to be seen whether respondent No.6 Mahbub Minhaj is a member of FBCCI or not. Admittedly, respondent No. 6 was not nominated by the BGMEA (Member Body/Ordinary Member) to the General Body of the Federation to be its general member. 'Such member' occurring in section 12 of the Ordinance in the context of the present case for the purpose of challenging FBCCI Election shall mean and include only the members of FBCCI and none else. Therefore, respondent No. 6 did not have the locus standi to file Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007. It is important to note here that the definition of member may vary from one trade organisation to another trade organisation. Respondent No. 6 may be a member of BGMEA but not a member of FBCCI. Again, he being a member of BGMEA could challenge its voter list before the Arbitration Tribunal but not against voter list of FBCCI of which he is neither an ordinary member nor a general member. 

 28. Another important aspect is that respondent No.6 filed Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of2007 without impleading BGMEA as a party although BGMEA is an ordinary member of FBCCI. Before the Tribunal, BGMEA is the most aggrieved party because its nominations were under challenge, before the Tribunal. In this connection, reliance may be made in the case of Md Abdul Naim vs Chairman, Board of Directors, Sonali Bank 1 MLR (AD) 106 = 1 BLC (AD) 80. It is held as follows: 

 29. Similar principle can be applied to the case in hand because the most aggrieved party BGMEA was not made a party to Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 2007. Therefore, we are of the view that BGMEA is not bound by the order/award passed by the Tribunal. In addition, though the facts of the case of Abdur Rashid vs Abdul Barik, 35 DLR (AD) 162 are distinguishable from those of the case in hand, the principle enunciated in the former case may be looked into. In that case, it is held that if a party satisfies a Court that summons were not duly served upon' him, the Court is bound to set aside the ex parte decree. In such a case. question of knowledge is not at all relevant and the ex parte decree will be set aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of the suit. 

 30. In the case in hand, BGMEA stated to have filed an application for addition of party and for adjournment on 25-9-2007. Respondent No. 2 (Arbitration Tribunal) in its affidavit-in-opposition stated "But since the Tribunal felt that BGMEA's adjournment application did not make any material difference on the issue before them and/or decision of the Tribunal, it rejected BGMEA's application for adjournment." The nomination made by the BGMEA was under challenge and therefore, its presence was indispensable before the Tribunal. But keeping the application for addition of party pending the Arbitration Tribunal passed the impugned order/award. From the above, it seems reasonably clear now that the haste precluded reasonable and deliberate judicial treatment of the case and was not warranted. 

 31. It is interesting to note here that respondent No. 2 (The Arbitration Tribunal) entered appearance in the case and contested it by filing an affidavit-in- opposition. It is not desirable that the Arbitration Tribunal supports its judgment or supports the case of the party in whose favour the award/order was passed. Arbitration Tribunal was made a party as a matter of practice. We disapprove of such a move of the Arbitration Tribunal. The rationale being that a Judge cannot defend his own judgment/decision. 

 32. Rule 16 of the Trade Organisation Rules, 1995 provides that if anybody has any objection regarding inclusion or deletion of the name of any person in the voter list, objection has to be filed within 6(six) days of publication of the voter list and that Appeal Board shall dispose of such objection within 3(three) days after hearing the parties. Therefore, it seems that finality has been attached to the decision of the Appeal Board. In the context of the present case, the Arbitration Tribunal should not have interfered with the decision of Appeal Board to which statutory finality has been attached. In the case in hand, the Arbitration Tribunal should have confined itself with FBCCI Election and not with BGMEA Election. If the election process is allowed to be thwarted at every stage, there will be no end of it. 

 33. Mr Ajmalul Hossain, learned Advocate, submits that interpretation of Article 14(i) is necessary in the context of the case in hand to determine whether the President and others of the Board of Directors had any responsibility in not holding the election in time. Article 14(iv) runs as under: 

 34. In the case in hand, the election could not be held because of the order of stay passed by the Court on 30-9-2007. Therefore, the President, the Vice-President and other members of the Board of Directors did not have any role in not holding the election within the stipulated time. As a result, they cannot be penalised for not holding the election within time. Therefore, disability mentioned in sub- article (iv) of Article 14 shall not apply to them.
